title: Introduce Lean Onramp Wizard: tenant-prefill presets + quantization validator
author: Arielle Chen
description: Context: onboarding tenants for Dedicated/Private often requires manual tuning of batch/cache defaults and quantization profiles. Teams repeatedly ask for safe, opinionated defaults that reduce cost without degrading tail accuracy. This PR introduces a lightweight "Lean Onramp Wizard" (CLI + Console hooks) that autogenerates tenant-prefill presets and runs a quantization validator simulation before recommending profiles. Motivation: reduce time-to-value for SRE/Customer Engineering during onboarding, and avoid regressions when we suggest aggressive int8/4-bit variants. Changes in this PR: 1) new CLI command `redwood onramp init --tenant <id>` that collects a small sample workload, runs a fast profiler, and emits a tenant-prefill preset (batch shapes, cache TTLs, per-route prefill thresholds) 2) quantization-validator: a local dry-run harness that applies candidate quant profiles (FP16, int8, int4 approximations) against a held-out prompt set and reports a small set of unit-econ metrics (mean latency, 90/95 latency, token cost delta, end-to-end quality delta) and a pass/fail verdict against tenant SLA thresholds 3) telemetry tagging: onramp presets emit structured telemetry with tags pref:tenant_onramp=v1, sample_hash and validation results for auditability 4) Console integration: an endpoint and UI payload (console API) that allows Customer Success to preview presets and force-apply with an approval workflow 5) safety gate: an opt-in conservative mode that will only recommend quant profiles if quality delta <= 0.6% (configurable) Rollout plan: feature gated behind `onramp:enabled` FF. Default behavior is read-only (no automatic live application) until ramped. Implementation notes: the CLI is implemented as a thin wrapper around an existing profiling library to avoid duplication. The quant-validator uses a lightweight sampling evaluator (200 prompts by default) and an embedding-based semantic similarity check + token-level diff heuristics to approximate quality regressions; exact evals are deferred to larger runs. Checklist: - [x] CLI plumbing and command docs - [x] quant-validator core harness + smoke tests - [x] telemetry tagging and Console preview API - [x] unit tests for serializer and CLI flags - [x] e2e smoke run against a synthetic tenant workload Manual testing: ran the onramp workflow against internal sandbox tenant `dev-tenant-12`; results: recommended batch size 8, prefill_ttl=30s, recommended quant profile: int8-stable with predicted token-cost -26% and quality delta +0.1% (pass). Related: ENG-3421 (onramp UX), ENG-3599 (quant-safety).

review_thread: Marco Silva (reviewer): Nice approach. A few questions: how do we ensure the sample is representative and not adversarial? Can we expose the sample size and seed to CEs?

Arielle Chen (author): Answer: CLI exposes --sample-size and --seed flags. Default sample_size=200 chosen from production-like traces (prior work with profiler). We added a sample_hash telemetry field so support can reproduce the exact sample.
Rhea Nambiar (reviewer): The quant-validator's similarity heuristic seems conservative; can we add a second metric based on logprob deltas?
Arielle Chen (author): Good suggestion — added a token-logprob-delta check as a secondary signal in validator, and tuned thresholds to avoid false positives on stable int8 profiles.
Tomás Ortega (reviewer): CI flaked once on the e2e smoke due to model availability. Suggest we mock network calls in unit tests and limit e2e to nightly for now.
Arielle Chen (author): Implemented a retry wrapper and a mock mode; updated CI job to run smoke in the "onramp-test" stage (non-blocking) and kept unit tests fast.
Marco Silva (reviewer): Approve after minor doc clarifications.
release_notes:
- Add 'redwood onramp init' to generate tenant-prefill presets and a quantization validation report.
- Console preview + approval workflow for safe application of presets.
- Telemetry tags for auditability of onramp runs.
Note: feature gated (onramp:enabled=false by default); visible to CEs after enabling.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps validator conservative; the goal is first to reduce operational toil. Future work: integrate with the larger eval harness for full-quality regression checks, and add auto-rollout with canary traffic split when a tenant opts-in.
changelog_hint: tools: onramp wizard (CLI + console preview) + quant-validator; no runtime change unless feature flag enabled
